title: incident-bot: oncall autodiagnostics - enhanced context & SLO hints
author: Priya Shah
description:
Motivation: On-call engineers often lack immediate, prioritized context in pagers that links SLO degradation signals to likely runbooks and recent operational actions (e.g. rollbacks, deploys). This PR enriches incident-bot autodiagnostics with SLO metadata, recent rollback/deploy history, and weighted runbook suggestions to reduce MTTR and triage time.

Changes: - Add a Context Enricher that merges SLO metadata (error budget burn, windowed latency percentiles) with service incident traces and recent deploy/rollback events. - Surface 'SLO hints' in the oncall message (e.g. probable cause buckets and confidence). - Prioritized runbook scoring: incorporate SLO relevance, past hit-rate, and recency. - Add a small in-memory cache and rate-limit for SLO metadata lookups to avoid query storms. - Feature flagged rollout via `autodiag-enhanced-context` (off by default).

Implementation notes: The enrichment happens as a post-processing step in bot/service/autodiag/context_enricher.py and calls the SLO toolkit via slo_toolkit/metadata_fetcher.py. Runbook scoring is implemented in runbooks/scoring.py with unit-tested heuristics. Message templates updated to include a compact SLO summary and top-3 prioritized runbook links. We added integration tests that run an end-to-end synthetic incident through the pipeline.

Rollout plan: behind boolean feature flag, staged rollout to 10% of oncall pages for 48h, monitor MTTR and pager burden metrics. If SLI regressions or noise increases, rollback by disabling flag.

Testing: unit tests added (tests/test_context_enricher.py), integration harness exercised in CI. Load-tested enrichment path to ensure <3ms median added latency for cached requests and <30ms for cold SLO fetches.

Related: ENG-9123 (autodiag improvements), ENG-9144 (oncall runbook prioritization).
